* Step 0.1 -- Inventory of the shipped tool surface

matching arm in =elot-gptel--tool-thunk=; every dispatcher arm has a

All 9 mutators now carry =:confirm t= (rename/move fixed in Step 1.2).

* Step 1.3 -- Error-contract table
CLOSED: [2026-07-13]

Audit of the failure contract of all 37 tools.  Verified that every
tool returns a single =ERROR:= (or, for the composite/never-raise
tools, a per-stage =FAIL at stage:=) line and never signals out to
gptel; that traversal-guard refusal is uniform; and that ROBOT-absent
refusal is uniform.

** Shared envelope (source of the contract)

- *Terminal handler.*  Read-only / DB / id tools end their body in the
  paired =condition-case= tail
  =(user-error (format "ERROR: %s" ...)) / (error (format "ERROR: %s" ...))=.
  No tool re-signals to gptel.
- *Mutating envelope.*  The six mutators routed through
  =elot-gptel-with-mutation= / =elot-gptel--apply-mutation=
  (=elot-gptel.el= ~l.4362) inherit the same =ERROR:= tail plus the
  write-back reports (=OK: ... / ERROR: revalidation failed -- changes
  rolled back=).
- *Traversal guard.*  Every file-taking tool resolves through
  =elot-gptel--resolve-file= / =--resolve-file-path= (~l.286 / l.311),
  which =user-error= with =elot-gptel: refusing path outside project:=
  / =elot-gptel: file not found:=.  Uniform.
- *ROBOT-absent.*  Identical string
  =elot-gptel: ROBOT not available -- set `elot-robot-jar-path'= at all
  7 sites (l.820 / 993 / 1146 / 1462 / 1688 / 1794 / 2156).  Uniform.
- *Side-effects gate.*  All four gate sites now converge on the
  =... refused -- side effects disabled (set `elot-gptel-allow-side-effects' ...)=
  wording (aligned in Step 1.3 -- see divergences below).

** Per-tool contract

RO envelope = =ERROR:= tail; MUT envelope = shared
=elot-gptel--apply-mutation= (=ERROR:= + rollback report).  "guard"
columns: T = routes through the traversal guard; R = has the uniform
ROBOT-absent refusal; G = honours the side-effects gate refusal.

** Divergences found and resolved (Step 1.3)

1. *=elot_edit_axioms= terminal =FAIL at= arm.*  The =user-error= arm of
   its =condition-case= tail returned =FAIL at %s= while its =error= arm
   and every sibling tool return =ERROR: %s=.  This was the only tool
   whose refusal/validation-error line diverged from the family
   envelope.  *Aligned* to =ERROR: %s= (l.5214).  The two tests that
   pinned the old =FAIL= prefix
   (=elot-gptel-edit-axioms-test-empty-edits=, and the unknown-op
   negative control at l.745) were updated to assert the =ERROR=
   prefix.  The intentional per-stage =FAIL at stage:= verdicts inside
   =elot_check= / =elot_axiom_check= are a *different, documented*
   contract (never-raise composite reports) and are left as-is.

2. *Side-effects gate wording drift.*  All four gate sites contained
   =refused= but only two said "side effects disabled":
   - =elot-gptel: mutation refused -- side effects disabled= (apply-mutation)
   - =elot-gptel: delete refused -- side effects disabled= (l.6415)
   - =elot-gptel: elot_db_remove_source refused -- mutating tool ...= (l.2507)
   - =elot-gptel: mutating SPARQL refused (set ...)= (l.1482)
   The last two were reworded to the canonical
   =... refused -- side effects disabled (set `elot-gptel-allow-side-effects' ...)=
   form so the refusal string is uniform across all gate sites.  These
   were not test-pinned, so the change is behaviour-visible only in the
   exact refusal wording.

No other stragglers: no tool signals raw out to gptel, and the
traversal-guard and ROBOT-absent refusals were already uniform.

** DONE byte-compile (clean)

*Canonical baseline = the =make byte-compile= target.*  The package
files legitimately =require= one another, so the authoritative build
compiles them together with the package dir on =load-path=:

: cd elot-package && emacs --batch -L . \
:   --eval "(setq byte-compile-error-on-warn nil)" \
:   -f batch-byte-compile <all *.el>

Run over all 16 files (elot-db, elot-defaults, elot-flymake,
elot-gptel, elot-id-insert, elot-id-move, elot-id-rename, elot-id,
elot-label-display, elot-lint, elot-mode, elot-owl-grammar, elot-robot,
elot-sources, elot-tangle, elot) it is *clean -- zero warnings, zero
errors*.  Real Step 0.2 build debt: *none*.

*** Isolated per-file runs (ARTEFACT, not the baseline)

The per-file =emacs -Q --batch -f batch-byte-compile FILE= run is
*not* a valid baseline: without =-L .= intra-package =require=s do not
resolve (e.g. elot-label-display.el errors with "Cannot open load
file: elot-tangle"), and without org preloaded the org-* references
show as undefined.  Load-path / load-order artefacts of compiling in
isolation, *not* real defects -- kept only for the record.

Captured on elot-gptel.el: 26 warnings in three classes -- all
disappear under the canonical =make byte-compile= run above:

- *Class A -- unused lexical =org-inhibit-startup= / =org-mode-hook=*
  (9 sites, 18 warnings): a =let= binds these two around org parsing but
  never references them in-scope.  Sites: elot-gptel--run-lint (407-408),
  --tangle-ontologies-to-workspace (633-634), --axiom-synthesise-draft
  (4077), --apply-mutation (4385), --axiom-find-rows (4567),
  --axiom-apply-edit (4613), tool-delete-resource (6446),
  tool-replace-with-parent (6663).  Real (harmless) dead bindings ->
  Phase 3 cleanup: either drop them or actually bind them via =dlet=/set.

- *Class B -- free variable* =elot-codelist-ht= in
  --slurp-label-context (1916): needs a =defvar= / =require= so the
  reference is declared.  Real -> Phase 3.

- *Class C -- "function ... not known to be defined"* (13 warnings, all
  =org-*= / =org-lint-*= at "end of data"): load-order artefact of
  compiling standalone without org loaded.  Not a bug, but Phase 3 should
  add =(require 'org)= / =(require 'org-lint)= / =(eval-when-compile
  (require 'org-element))= or explicit =declare-function= to silence.

** DONE package-lint (no actionable debt)

=package-lint-current-buffer= on elot-gptel.el reports 313 issues, but
they are *all* of the "you should depend on (emacs \"NN\")" family
(lexical-binding, cl-lib, subr-x, string-empty-p, ...).  These are
false positives here: the package's dependency floor is declared in
elot.el with =;; Package-Requires: ((emacs "30.1"))=, which subsumes
every version package-lint asks for.  package-lint flags them because
it is run against elot-gptel.el in isolation rather than the package's
main file.  *No actionable package-lint debt* -> Phase 3 need only
confirm the header is read from elot.el.

** Bucket 2 -- red today (P0, must be green before merge)

The bucket-4 run (make -k, all ~40 targets) surfaced *9 failing tests*
across *4 targets*, clustering into *3 root causes*:

*** Cluster A -- child insert under an individual: WANTED (author-chosen subheading relation) -- RESOLVED (tests rewritten)

- gptel-insert-test: elot-gptel-insert-test-child-refused-under-individual
- id-insert-test:    elot-id-insert-test-child-refused-individual-resource

Original diagnosis (superseded): inserting a child under an individual
was read as a missing guard, since individuals cannot have
subclasses/subproperties.

*Reframed by maintainer (2026-07-12):* NOT a defect -- the behaviour is
*wanted*.  Nesting one individual under another in the Org outline
authors an object-property relation between them.  The *author chooses*
which object property applies to sub-headings via a heading property,
e.g.:

#+begin_example
:PROPERTIES:
:ELOT-subheading-relation: skos:broader
:END:
#+end_example

SKOS =broader= is the initial and likely most common use case, but the
mechanism is general -- any object property may be chosen, for other
applications too.  So accepting a child under an individual is
*correct*, and the two tests that expect a refusal are the thing that
is wrong.

*Action:* the current tool/insert behaviour (accept) is retained.  The
two failing tests
  - =elot-gptel-insert-test-child-refused-under-individual=
  - =elot-id-insert-test-child-refused-individual-resource=
should be *deleted or rewritten* to assert that a child under an
individual is *accepted* (ideally with a positive test that sets
=:ELOT-subheading-relation:= and checks the resulting object-property
nesting).  The datatype guard is unaffected (datatypes genuinely
cannot take children -- that guard stays).

This flips Cluster A from "fix the code" to "fix the tests"; net effect
still clears both reds.  Phase 1 slice.

*RESOLVED (Phase 1):* the two refusal tests were replaced by positive
tests asserting a child under an individual is *accepted*:
  - =elot-gptel-insert-test-child-refused-under-individual= ->
    =elot-gptel-insert-test-child-allowed-under-individual=
  - =elot-id-insert-test-child-refused-individual-resource= ->
    =elot-id-insert-test-child-allowed-under-individual=
Tool/insert behaviour unchanged; datatype guard untouched.

*CONFIRMED GREEN (2026-07-12):* live run of =make gptel-insert-test
id-insert-test= passed 36 resp. 34 tests, 0 unexpected.  Cluster A is
CLOSED.

*** Cluster B -- edit-axiom(s) result-contract drift (6 tests)

- gptel-edit-axiom-test:  elot-gptel-edit-axiom-test-rollback-on-lint-fail
- gptel-edit-axioms-test: atomic-on-bad-edit, dry-run-bypasses-gate,
  empty-fragment-ambiguous-among-empties, rollback-on-lint-fail,
  side-effects-disabled

Every failure is a *prefix / wording mismatch* between what the tool
returns and what the test asserts:

| test expects prefix        | tool now returns                                  |
|----------------------------+---------------------------------------------------|
| FAIL:                      | ERROR: revalidation failed -- changes rolled back |
| FAIL at edits[N]:          | ERROR: edits[N]: ...                              |
| FAIL (side-effects)        | ERROR: elot-gptel: mutation refused -- ...        |
| OK: dry-run applied N edits | OK: applied N edits  (dry_run: file unchanged...) |

The tool bodies were evidently re-worded (ERROR:/OK: applied ...) but
the tests still assert the older FAIL:/dry-run wording.  Needs a
*decision in Step 1.3* (error-path uniformity): pick the canonical
prefixes, then align tool or tests.  Not a behaviour bug -- the tools
do the right thing (rollback, refusal, dry-run) -- but a contract the
tests pin to the old strings.  P0 (red), low-risk fix.

*RESOLVED (2026-07-12): aligned the tests, not the tools.*  The
=ERROR:= / =OK: applied ...= envelope is already the family-wide
canonical contract -- the delete/insert/move/rename tests all assert
=ERROR: revalidation failed -- changes rolled back=, and their tool
bodies (via the shared =elot-gptel--apply-mutation=) emit it.  The
edit-axiom(s) tests were the only outliers still pinned to the
pre-refactor =FAIL:= / =dry-run applied= wording.  Six assertions
updated: =elot-gptel-edit-axiom-test.el= (rollback-on-lint-fail) and
=elot-gptel-edit-axioms-test.el= (atomic-on-bad-edit,
rollback-on-lint-fail, side-effects-disabled, dry-run-bypasses-gate,
empty-fragment-ambiguous-among-empties).  Tool bodies unchanged.
*CONFIRMED GREEN (2026-07-12):* live run of =make gptel-edit-axiom-test
gptel-edit-axioms-test= passed 11 resp. 19 tests, 0 unexpected.

* DONE Step 0.4 -- dependency-posture findings

Read-only audit; no code changed.  Per posture:

- *gptel is a soft dependency: CONFIRMED.* elot-gptel.el declares the
  gptel entry points via `declare-function' and pulls gptel only at
  tool *registration*: `elot-gptel-register-tools' calls
  (require 'gptel nil 'noerror) and `user-error's with an install hint
  when gptel is absent (elot-gptel.el ~l.8711-8713);
  `elot-gptel-unregister-tools' guards on (featurep 'gptel); and the
  `elot-gptel-confirm-mutations' setter re-registers only
  (when (featurep 'gptel) ...).  There is no top-level (require 'gptel).
  The analogous optional-deps load contract is covered by
  test/elot-load-without-sparql-test.el, which shadows optional
  packages unavailable in a child Emacs and asserts a clean load.
- *ROBOT is optional: CONFIRMED.* `elot-robot-available-p' is a cheap
  cached filesystem / exec-path probe (no JVM spawn); `elot-robot-run'
  signals a clean `user-error' "ROBOT not available -- set
  `elot-robot-jar-path' or install `robot' on PATH" rather than
  crashing, and returns non-zero exits / timeouts in its result plist
  for callers to classify.  ROBOT-absent degradation is exercised
  across 11 test files: reasoning-test, omn-validate-test,
  sparql-tool-test, gptel-check-test, gptel-diff-test,
  gptel-omn-report-test, sources-test, sources-ttl-lang-test,
  sparql-roundtrip-test, robot-test, ttl-prefix-test.
- *Single ROBOT process layer in elot-robot.el: VIOLATIONS (legacy
  paths).* elot-robot.el is the intended argv-based layer
  (`elot-robot-run' via make-process / call-process[-region]), but
  ROBOT is still invoked directly outside it in deprecated code:
  elot.el `elot-robot-execute-query' uses (call-process "java" ...
  "-jar" elot-robot-jar-path ...) (~l.260) and the deprecated
  `elot-robot-command' uses `shell-command' (~l.384); elot-tangle.el
  `elot-robot-omn-to-ttl--batch' uses `call-process' (~l.400) and
  `elot-robot-omn-to-ttl--interactive' uses `make-process' (~l.444).
  These predate `elot-robot-run' and are not yet routed through it, so
  the single-layer posture is not fully met.  No stray
  `shell-command-to-string' anywhere; the only "robot"/process-spawn
  sites are the ones listed.  Migrating the four legacy call sites onto
  `elot-robot-run' is a follow-up (not in Phase 0 scope).

This closes Phase 0.
